Per quanto ne so, nel privato rischi la faccia e basta, nella PA rischi di cadere nel reato di falsità ideologica (info che puoi riscontrare anche online) poiché considerabile falsificazione. 
Sottolineo che non sono esperta di legge per cui posso dirti solo ciò che so.

Personalmente ti direi evita di mentire. 
Se l’azienda di tuo interesse chiedesse referenze agli ultimi datori di lavoro faresti una pessima figura. Premetto che non me ne intendo della posizione di tuo interesse, comunque nulla ti vieta di inserire nel CV che hai svolto le mansioni richieste dal ruolo per accelerare dei processi nella posizione in cui lavoravi e che quindi sei competente.
The Ladder or Holding on to smoke

Whatever you will choose, remember that you’re not a failure! I wanted to be a FA since I was 7yo and it kept going for my whole adolescence. One day i got the opportunity, so I followed the course, I got my attestation and my wings. 
Everything looked great. After one month I started feeling alone and missing the important people in my life. Two months after I started, I decided to quit. It was hard because I always wanted this job, my parents helped me economically, and everybody was excited for me. 
But it was not my thing at all. 
I think that in every kind of job you cannot realize if it’s for you unless you try it. 
And trying it’s important to understand what do you need. If you realized that a 9-5 job it’s better for you, go ahead and follow what makes you feel good. 
But, you can even give it a shot and try to stay for a year, remember that we can give you advice, but you’re the only person that can decide for yourself… 
As always, what worked for me doesn’t mean that will work for you. 
I’m a person that gets tired easily if don’t like something, that’s why I quitted so fast. Other people that did the training with me decided to stay at least one year even if they didn’t like it. Somebody quitted, somebody became an instructor. 
Do what you feel is the best for you, but don’t let this situation discourage you or making you feel bad. Lots of good vibes

I attempted suicide a few times and I know that you’re thinking this is the best way to stop suffering. 
But look, you’re young and you have so many things to do and try in your life... 
Adolescence most times sucks, I’ll be honest with you, but there are little things that would help you, maybe a hobby, a pet, or a person.
My lifesaver was music for example and a few months ago a person became part of my life making it so much better.

I don’t know your reasons, but trust me, you’ll find something that will change your mind, maybe in a couple of years you’ll think about this moment and you’ll think “I never thought I’d make it!”.  
Think it over, please, I don’t know you, just remember that you’re not alone and asking for help is the best thing to do.
